query: Help me understand what's worth attention in these incident descriptions.

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents by type (wifi, vpn, database, etc.) is a strong grouping axis directly answering what's worth attention. Values are sound readings of short_description across all samples.

per_column.name: affected_system_component
per_column.rationale: A finer-grained component axis adds some analytical leverage beyond category. Largely aligned with category and text, but distinguishing e.g. 'vpn_client' vs 'vpn_server', 'database_server' vs 'mysql' often infers specifics the short text may not state; mostly warranted but some confident specifics.

per_column.name: failure_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Symptom type (connection_failure, access_denied, outage) is a useful axis for triaging attention. Values track the text well ('Cannot connect'->connection_failure, 'Unable to access'->access_denied), and a NULL/Unknown for the vague 'Printing issues' row is correct behavior.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual/system_wide/location_specific) is highly relevant for prioritizing attention. However short_descriptions like 'Unable to connect to the office VPN' rarely state scope; assigning 'individual_user' vs 'system_wide' is often an unsupported confident inference from silent text.

per_column.name: self_resolved_indicator
per_column.rationale: Whether an incident self-resolved could be useful, but the provided source text (short_description, opened_at, closed_by) gives no basis for a true/false self-resolution flag; the values appear invented rather than derived.

per_column.name: cross_assigned_indicator
per_column.rationale: Cross-assignment could be derived from assigned_to vs assignment_group/closed_by, so it is potentially grounded and mildly useful, but the evidence samples don't clearly support the specific true/false values, suggesting weak grounding.

per_column.name: opened_hour_bucket
per_column.rationale: Bucketing opened_at into business/evening/night is a legitimate temporal axis for spotting patterns. Directly and correctly derived from the opened_at timestamp in every sample.

per_column.name: recurrence_within_period
per_column.rationale: Recurrence flags are valuable for identifying what warrants attention, and could in principle be computed from repeated descriptions/callers. But grounding is uncertain from single-row text; values may not be reliably derivable, with borderline support in samples.

judge.rationale: Most added columns provide genuine grouping/comparison axes (category, component, symptom, scope, time bucket) well-suited to surfacing what deserves attention, so table-level usefulness is high. Grounding is mixed: text-derived columns (incident_category, failure_symptom_type, opened_hour_bucket) are well supported, but several behavioral/scope flags (self_resolved_indicator, scope_indicator, cross_assigned_indicator, recurrence_within_period) assert specifics not clearly supported by the available source text, pulling groundedness down.
